scope: Proposition 5.5 (Selection of profile pairs) of the manuscript “The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture” (preprints/The-higher-dimensional-Erdos-distinct-distances-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 166 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 37f6355365a18510), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every p ∈ P, let Cp be a finite family of irreducible projective curves in Pd−1, each spanning a projective subspace of dimension at most two, with total degree at most E = δN/A. Suppose that 1 − o(1) of the unordered pairs {p, q} satisfy πp(q) ∈ Cp or πq(p) ∈ Cq. After the global terminal deletion described below, one of the following configurations occurs. 1. A core of positive relative size is covered. 2. Two sequences of non-core pieces have a common dyadic width s, the same limiting profile, and an ordered product covered in one orientation with positive relative density. 3. Two sequences of non-core pieces have widths with ratio tending to infinity, both o(log B), the same limiting profile, and such a positively covered ordered product. In the common outermost window s = log B, the two factors may instead be the same pool of pieces in a shrinking profile bin. That pool has size n ≥ N √ δ, is the union of exp(o(s)) pieces, and retains all the preceding degree, mass, regularity, and product-testing conclusions to exponential accuracy. All selected incidences may be required to lie on physical lines containing at most Bo(1) sample points. The global terminal deletion means the following. Whenever a target point was assigned to its carrier curve after the (d − 1)st cut, its projection from the center is not a curve contained in the center’s directional family.
